title: Mac and Cheese
description: Stovetop mac with a sodium citrate cheese sauce built on evaporated milk, extra-sharp cheddar and aged Gruyère, with low-moisture mozzarella folded in at the end for pull. Holds overnight without breaking, so it doubles as a make-ahead holiday side.
source: Jack's own, built on the sodium citrate method from Modernist Cuisine

notes: Assumes 12 g for the 2 tsp miso and 15 g for the 1 tbsp Dijon (USDA has no Dijon entry, so it uses prepared yellow mustard). Counts the cheddar as sharp cheddar.
Pasta is counted dry. The pasta water, sodium citrate and spices are left out.

ingredients.label: Evaporated milk
ingredients.sourceLabel: USDA SR28, NDB 01214: MILK,CND,EVAP,WO/ ADDED VIT A & VITAMIN D

ingredients.label: Low-moisture mozzarella
ingredients.sourceLabel: USDA SR28, NDB 01027: CHEESE,MOZZARELLA,WHL MILK,LO MOIST

directions.title: Pasta
directions.text: Boil the {elbows} elbows in unsalted water until 2–3 minutes short of the box time (go the full 3 if you're making it ahead). Reserve {pasta-water} of the pasta water, then drain. Don't rinse the pasta.

directions.title: Sauce base
directions.text: In the empty pot over medium-low, whisk the {evap} evaporated milk, {pasta-water} reserved pasta water, {miso} miso, {dijon} Dijon and {citrate} sodium citrate until the miso and Dijon are dispersed and the citrate is dissolved.

directions.title: Melt the cheese
directions.text: Add the {cheddar} cheddar and {gruyere} Gruyère a handful at a time, stirring constantly until each batch melts in. Keep it below a simmer, or the cheese will brown onto the bottom of the pot and be a pain to scrub out.

directions.title: Season
directions.text: Off the heat, stir in the {garlic} garlic powder, {onion} onion powder, {cayenne} cayenne, {white-pepper} white pepper and {nutmeg} nutmeg. Taste, and salt only if it needs it.

directions.title: Combine
directions.text: Dump all the pasta into the sauce and mix thoroughly. If it's tight, loosen it with a splash of water at a time.

directions.title: Make ahead (optional)
directions.text: Pour it into a 9×13 and chill uncovered, then cover with foil once it's cold. To serve, bake covered at 350°F until the center hits 165°F, about 45–60 minutes, stirring once halfway.

directions.title: Finish
directions.text: Fold the {mozz} mozzarella into the hot mac right before serving.

notes: The salt comes almost entirely from the sodium citrate and the cheese, which is why the pasta water stays unsalted.
Mozzarella goes in at the end, never before chilling: leftover citrate in the sauce strips its calcium overnight and kills the stretch.
No need to grate. Chunks melt fine in a citrate sauce.
Mustard powder works in place of the Dijon at a third of the volume, bloomed in cold water for 10 minutes.

deviations.what: Sodium citrate holds the sauce instead of a roux
deviations.why: Stays smooth through chilling and reheating, and there's no flour muting the cheese.

deviations.what: Evaporated milk and starchy pasta water instead of a milk béchamel
deviations.why: The evaporated milk gives the sauce body without any flour, and the starch in the pasta water helps it cling to the noodles.

deviations.what: Miso and Dijon in the sauce
deviations.why: Savory depth that reads as better cheese, not as its own flavor.

deviations.what: Low-moisture mozzarella folded in at the end
deviations.why: A citrate sauce has no stretch on its own. The mozz brings the pull back.
The citrate and cheese already bring all the salt.

log.entry: Round 1, made ahead and baked the next day. Water plus evaporated milk, 22 g citrate, plain sharp cheddar, Tillamook blend and young Gruyère. Good but boring, and the sauce pooled at the bottom overnight.

Round 2. Swapped the 1½ cups of plain water for a cup of pasta water, cut citrate to 18 g, switched to extra-sharp cheddar and aged Gruyère, unsalted pasta water, mozzarella folded in at the end. Kicks ass.
